page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e4.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 cores with hyper-threading enabled. Operating at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance is configured with a shared CPU allocation. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations reveal a performance profile characterized by average multi-core capabilities alongside weaker single-core execution. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance falls into the bottom 10%, while the multi-core score of 7603.91 sits in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth is moderate, with read-only large block transfers reaching 48.82 GB/sec and write speeds at 33.48 GB/sec. Cryptographic and compression tasks show some limitations, as evidenced by a weak PassMark encryption score of 2316.78 and a poor single-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 7.36 GB/sec. However, the instance demonstrates solid throughput for standard web operations, achieving 9.13 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and 8.41 GB/sec in static web serving.

From a resource density perspective, the ecs.e4.2xlarge offers a cost-effective profile for memory-intensive workloads that do not require dedicated CPU resources or high-speed local NVMe storage. The shared CPU allocation and older Intel Broadwell architecture represent a clear tradeoff, resulting in lower single-threaded compute efficiency and reduced performance in complex tasks like LLM inference, where text generation for a 7B model drops to 4.61 tokens/sec. Consequently, this instance is best suited for memory-heavy but compute-moderate workloads, such as caching layers, Redis deployments, static web serving, and general-purpose database hosting where high memory capacity is prioritized over raw processing speed.
